patronOf.en-US: St. Maurice and his soldiers, martyrs
patronOf.pt-BR: São Maurício e seus soldados, mártires

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Thank God for every slight and injury you have to bear. An injury borne in meekness and silence is a true victory.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Agradece a Deus por cada desprezo e injúria que tens de suportar. Uma injúria suportada em mansidão e silêncio é uma verdadeira vitória.

meta.face: Three clearly different men of Upper Egypt. MAURICE (centre), about forty, with DEEP-BROWN skin as in the Magdeburg statue: a LONG OVAL face with a HIGH, rounded forehead, HIGH, PROMINENT cheekbones, a BROAD, straight nose with rounded nostrils, full, well-drawn lips, large, calm dark eyes under straight black brows, a strong, ROUNDED chin; short, tightly curled black hair and a SHORT, close black beard along the jaw; the gaze steady and serene. EXUPERIUS (left), about fifty-five, warm olive-brown: a SQUARE, heavy-browed face with a strong, HOOKED nose, deep-set dark eyes, a wide, thin mouth and a SHORT, grizzled grey-black beard; close-cropped grey hair. CANDIDUS (right), about twenty-two, light-brown, BEARDLESS: a NARROW, TRIANGULAR face with a small, pointed chin, a straight, fine nose, large almond-shaped dark eyes lifted upward, short, straight black hair. Not the beardless young charles_lwanga, the round benedito, or the old, hooded Egyptians paphnutius and macarius_alexandria.
meta.basis: Eucherius of Lyon's account, which the Martyrology follows, names Maurice, Exuperius and Candidus at Agaunum under Maximian. The legion came from the Thebaid in Egypt; Maurice has been shown as a dark-skinned African since the Magdeburg statue of about 1240 (Wikipedia), which the card follows. The companions' faces are ours.
